name: Becher
overview: Becher was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as a son of Benjamin. He is mentioned in the biblical record as part of the list of "sons of Israel" who journeyed to Egypt during the patriarchal period. His inclusion in this genealogical record situates him within the foundational history of Israel's tribes.
namesAndTitles: The name Becher is a proper name meaning "young male camel." This meaning reflects a common practice in Hebrew naming, though the name itself was not given by God. The significance of the name lies primarily in its literal meaning rather than any divine attribution.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Becher as a son of Benjamin. Additional inferred relationships from 1 Chronicles 7:8 suggest connections to individuals such as Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth, though these are not explicitly stated as direct family but may represent descendants or related clan members.
scriptureSignificance: Becher's importance in the biblical narrative is primarily genealogical, as he is listed among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, marking a pivotal moment in Israel's history that led to the Israelites' eventual sojourn and deliverance. His inclusion underscores the continuity of the tribe of Benjamin and contributes to the broader understanding of Israel's tribal composition during the patriarchal era.
